title: Build each thread backward
statement: Build each concept thread backward from a demanding end point, keeping the concept constant and raising the difficulty, so a later stage on the same content always asks for more.
example: One standards set lifted two Grade 8 history standards from explain and describe to evaluate, so they ask more than the Grade 7 standards on the same content.
detail: A text-sourcing brief builds each thread from a Grade 8 destination: it names the concept that text demands, chooses earlier texts that build the same concept in simpler form every year, and keeps the concept constant while the difficulty rises (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Curriculum maps/1. Mapping Docs/Copy of DevFactory_Example_Backward-Design_Threads.docx`). A whole-course thematic map tracks the complexity of each idea on rungs alongside grade (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Curriculum maps/1. Mapping Docs/Grade_3-12_Full_Thematic_Map.xlsx`). A social studies standards set lifted two Grade 8 history standards, explain to evaluate and describe to evaluate, so their demand is strictly higher than that of the Grade 7 standards on the same content (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx`). These are design rules; no outcome was measured.

evidence.quote: We pick a Grade 8 destination, name the concept it demands, then choose earlier texts that build that same concept in simpler form every year.
Keep the concept constant, raise the difficulty.
